title: Durotar
body: Durotar is a hard country of red rock, scrub and baking heat on the eastern shore of Kalimdor, and it is the homeland Thrall claimed for the orcs after the battle at Mount Hyjal. He named it for his father, Durotan, and raised its great city, Orgrimmar, in the northern mountains. The land was not empty when the orcs came. Razormane quilboar held much of it and still lurk behind their brambles, Kolkar centaurs camp in the southern crags, and Dustwind harpies plunder the caravans. Soldiers of Kul Tiras, left behind when Admiral Proudmoore fell, hold a keep on the eastern coast, and the demon cult of the Burning Blade hides in caves and gorges from the Valley of Trials to the very walls of the capital. The Darkspear trolls, sworn allies of the Horde, share the land from Sen'jin Village, exiled from their Echo Isles by the witch doctor Zalazane. At Razor Hill, Gar'Thok keeps watch over it all.

title: Valley of Trials
body: Hemmed in by red cliffs in the south of Durotar, the Valley of Trials is where young orcs and trolls come of age. Kaltunk greets each recruit and sends them on to Gornek, who keeps to the Den, a cave cut into the valley's heart where trainers of every calling wait. Mottled boars root to the north, scorpid workers swarm the slopes, and peons gather lumber from the few trees that grow here, when they are not caught napping. Even this proving ground is not clean: imps and felstalkers spill from a cave in the northern cliffs, where the Burning Blade has made a coven of its own.

title: Burning Blade Coven
body: The caves in the northern cliffs of the Valley of Trials were once just caves. Foreman Thazz'ril surveyed them for ore and left his favorite pick in a chamber of waterfalls, only to return and find the place full of vicious beasts. The Burning Blade had moved in. Vile familiars and felstalkers now creep out into the valley, and deep inside, the warlock Yarrog Baneshadow guards a medallion of dark power. That a demon cult dares to nest beside the Horde's own training ground is a warning that it has wider designs on Durotar.

title: Spirit Rock
body: Southwest of the Valley of Trials, at the end of a narrow way the shaman call the Hidden Path, stands Spirit Rock. It is holy ground. Here young orc and troll shaman drink the earth sapta, a draught that binds the spirit to an element, for such a drink may only be taken in a sacred place. Those who drink it see what others cannot: the earth itself stands before them as a living presence and judges whether they are ready. Earth spirits of red stone linger nearby.

title: Sen'jin Village
body: When Zalazane's dark voodoo drove them from the Echo Isles, the free Darkspear trolls built Sen'jin Village on the strand of southern Durotar, and named it for Sen'jin, Vol'jin's father, the chieftain slain by murlocs on the isles where the tribe first met Thrall. The old witch doctor Master Gadrin speaks for the village, with his assistant Bom'bay at his side, while the hunter Vel'rin Fang trades in tiger hides, the alchemist Master Vornal, whose eyes are failing, tests would be apprentices, and the scout Lar Prowltusk watches the western flank for centaurs. A raptor handler and a mage of the tribe make their homes here too.

title: Echo Isles
body: The Echo Isles off Durotar's southern coast were the Darkspear's first home in Kalimdor, and they are lost to them now. The witch doctor Zalazane rules the largest isle from among his huts, surrounded by trolls he has hexed and bound to his will. In a circle of power on the largest isle he keeps a ring of skulls, one of them holding the trapped spirit of a slain Darkspear, and tainted fetishes called ju-ju heaps foul the flow of magic across the land. Yet the wild life of the isles goes on: Durotar tigers hunt in the shade of the trees, bloodtalon raptors bury their eggs in the sand, and makrura and crawlers crowd the shallows.

title: Kolkar Crag
body: Over the ridge west of Sen'jin Village lies Kolkar Crag, a gorge where Kolkar centaurs have made their camp. They are not content to stay there. The scout Lar Prowltusk crept into the camp during one of their raids and learned that the centaurs mean to strike Durotar in three places at once: the Valley of Trials, Sen'jin Village and the gates of Orgrimmar itself. Each plan is held by a different leader of the camp, and the whole host answers to Warlord Kolkanis. The trolls and orcs would likely win such a war, but at a cost in blood they would rather not pay.

title: Razor Hill
body: Razor Hill stands at the crossroads of central Durotar, an orc town under the command of Gar'Thok, whose barracks is the largest building in the place. Soon after the orcs came to these shores, Kul Tiran agents lured Thrall to a false parley here, and it was Rexxar who went in his stead and defeated the assassins waiting there. Today recruits fresh from the Valley pass through on their way into the wider land. Orgnil Soulscar hunts demon cultists from here, an old veteran watches from the tower with his signal horn, and the inn offers a fire and a place to boast of battles.

title: Tiragarde Keep
body: Admiral Daelin Proudmoore built this keep on Durotar's eastern coast when he brought the fleet of Kul Tiras against the orcs. The Horde broke his offensive and the keep fell, and the admiral himself died at Theramore. But his reserves under Lieutenant Benedict came back and took it again, and Kul Tiran sailors and marines now hold the walls with Watch Commander Zalaphil keeping guard. To the orcs this is a betrayal of the pact Thrall made with Jaina Proudmoore against Archimonde, and the keep sits like a splinter in the side of their homeland.

title: Scuttle Coast
body: Along the shore north and east of Tiragarde Keep, the rocks are littered with the bones of Proudmoore's fleet, broken on the rocks during the war with the Horde. The wrecks still hold their stores, and among them lie toolboxes of gnomish make, full of the clever devices the Alliance uses to build its machines. Gar'Thok wants them hauled ashore and sent to Orgrimmar so the Horde may learn how its enemies work. Salvagers must reckon with the makrura and surf crawlers that scuttle along the beach, and with the sand sharks that patrol the waters beyond.

title: Razormane Grounds
body: West of Razor Hill, where brambles sprout from the red hills and old bones bleach in the sun, the Razormane quilboar still cling to Durotar. When the orcs arrived the quilboar held much of this land, and though the orcs have driven out most of them, their fortified camps here keep spitting out scouts, dustrunners and battleguards. Geolord Mottle, who wraps himself in lightning and mends wounds with healing waves, leads among them with Captain Flat Tusk of the battleguard. Gar'Thok will allow the quilboar no hold at all on orc land, and he dreams of one day clearing them from the whole of Kalimdor.

title: Shrine of the Dormant Flame
body: From the banks of the Southfury, before the river meets the sea, a hidden trail winds up one of the highest peaks in Durotar. At the summit is the Shrine of the Dormant Flame, most holy to the shaman of the Horde. Its keeper, the troll Telf Joolam, turns away the treasure seekers who climb up expecting riches and find only an empty shrine. To shaman who come bearing the proper torch he reveals its secret: after drinking the fire sapta, they may see and face the flame's manifestation at the peak, and kindle their torch at its brazier.

title: Southfury River
body: The Southfury River runs down from the north to the sea and marks Durotar's western border with the Barrens, with the orc garrison of Far Watch Post standing just across. Its banks are the hunting grounds of the dreadmaw crocolisks, and they have claimed at least one proud young hunter. Misha Tor'kren's son Kron went west to hunt them and never came home. Along its lower reaches, near where the river meets the Great Sea, a hidden trail climbs to the Shrine of the Dormant Flame.

title: Tor'kren Farm
body: Tor'kren Farm is a modest pig farm in northwestern Durotar, below Thunder Ridge, worked by the orc Misha Tor'kren. She once kept it with her son Kron, a strong youth whose stubborn pride got him into trouble. When she warned him that the crocolisks of the Southfury were too dangerous, he stormed off west to hunt them, and days passed without word. Misha waits at the farm still, wanting at least some sign of his fate so she can begin to mourn, and keeping a gift she had meant to give him on his return.

title: Thunder Ridge
body: Thunder Ridge is a gorge in northwestern Durotar, southwest of Orgrimmar, where herds of thunder lizards and crackling lightning hides roam. It was once wooded, until human loggers began stripping it in the first days of the orcs' settlement. Now the Burning Blade has come. The goblin warlock Fizzle Darkstorm keeps a camp in the ridge with fanatics and apprentices of the cult, spreading chaos from it, and Orgnil Soulscar of Razor Hill wants him dead. Horde warriors also come here to prove their toughness against the lizards.

title: Razorwind Canyon
body: A long canyon runs through the hills north of Razor Hill, and the supply caravans that use it have learned to fear it. Dustwind harpies swoop from the walls, pillage the wagons and leave the stolen sacks strewn about their roosts. Rezlak of the Tinkers' Union, one of Gazlowe's goblins sent to help the orcs build, lost his last shipment this way and can get nothing done without it. Through the canyon's eastern side lies Drygulch Ravine, where the harpies nest in greater numbers still.

title: Drygulch Ravine
body: Drygulch Ravine is a deep cleft reached through the eastern side of Razorwind Canyon, and it is the true nest of the Dustwind harpies. Savages and storm witches of the flock hold its floor and cliffs, and as long as they thrive no caravan in the region is safe. Rezlak of the Tinkers' Union would see every one of them dead. The harpies are not the only danger. In Dustwind Cave, high above the ravines, cultists of the Burning Blade gather with neophytes and thugs of the cult, and they too carry its searing collars.

title: Skull Rock
body: Skull Rock is a cave in the mountains just east of Orgrimmar, close enough to the capital to alarm anyone who learns what lies inside. It shelters the largest band of the Burning Blade in Durotar. Within, the cultists perform their rites and burn their own flesh with searing collars, which seem to attune them to demonic power. The orc warlock Gazz'uz leads them, and a rarely seen felweaver called Scornn stalks the tunnels. Warlocks of the cult have even stolen from the Horde's own warlocks and hidden their prize here.

title: Rocktusk Farm
body: Rocktusk Farm is a pig farm on the western road out from Orgrimmar's gates, where swine root in their pens under the walls of the capital. The venomtail scorpids that hunt near the city entrance are among the deadliest in Durotar, as the Darkspear Rhinag learned when he hunted them without an antidote and one stung him deeply. Too weak to return to Sen'jin and too ashamed to want to, he now waits here for an antidote from Kor'ghan of the Cleft of Shadow, dreading the further rituals Kor'ghan will put him through once he recovers.

title: Gar'Thok
body: Gar'Thok commands Razor Hill and greets visitors with little patience for talk and much for work. In the first days of Durotar he was at an orc outpost when sailors of Kul Tiras fell on it and slaughtered his men. He survived, and he has not forgotten. He never trusted the humans even while fighting beside them, and he sends young warriors against the Kul Tiran holdouts at Tiragarde Keep and to salvage gnomish tools from Proudmoore's wrecks. He means to clear the Razormane from Durotar as well.

title: Orgnil Soulscar
body: Orgnil Soulscar is the orc who polices Durotar against evils of the spirit, and above all against the Burning Blade. He keeps watch from Razor Hill, and he swears that no servant of demons will be suffered in the land. When word reached him that the cult had crept into the Valley of Trials, his alarm was plain: the Burning Blade was spreading. He tracked down the warlock Fizzle Darkstorm in Thunder Ridge, and he turns to the shaman Margoz for counsel on the cult's deeper secrets.

title: Master Gadrin
body: Master Gadrin is the aged witch doctor who speaks for Sen'jin Village, and he bids those who would talk with him to come and sit at his side. His grief is personal. Zalazane took his brother Minshina and killed him, then chained the spirit inside its own skull, and Gadrin hears it calling to him in his dreams. He wants Zalazane's reign over the Echo Isles ended so that the tribe can sleep in peace. Behind him his assistant Bom'bay, working his way through witch doctor school, mends the ailing, and Gadrin's knowledge of troll lore runs deep enough that he knows the whispered true name of the Witherbark spider god.

title: Zalazane
body: Zalazane is a witch doctor of the Darkspear who turned on his own tribe. When the trolls settled the Echo Isles after helping the Horde against Proudmoore, he used dark voodoo to rob most of them of their will and bend them to his service, and the free Darkspear had to abandon the isles for the mainland. He was not content to let them go. From his huts on the largest isle he sends hexed trolls across the water to drag more of his kin under his sway. He killed Gadrin's brother Minshina and chained the spirit in its skull, and his tainted ju-ju heaps foul the flow of magic across Durotar.

title: Lieutenant Benedict
body: Lieutenant Benedict commands the reserves of Kul Tiras that Admiral Proudmoore left behind. After the admiral's death and the fall of Tiragarde Keep, Benedict brought his men back and retook it, and he holds it still with sailors and marines who guard his belongings jealously. To the orcs he is the living proof that humans honor no treaty. In a chest he keeps close lie sealed orders under the admiral's own seal, showing that Proudmoore's plans were laid well before his death and that more of his men may yet land on Durotar's shores.

title: Margoz
body: Margoz is an orc shaman who keeps a camp in northeastern Durotar, between the coast and Drygulch Ravine. He knows more of the Burning Blade's corruption than most, and Orgnil Soulscar values his counsel. Margoz believes the cultists' searing collars bind them to demonic power, and he has tried to read their secrets in a trance, only to be burned by the magic he unleashed. Admitting the task is beyond a shaman, he sends the collars to the warlock Neeru Fireblade in Orgrimmar, uneasy about whether Neeru's craft is as harmless as he claims.

title: Gazz'uz
body: Gazz'uz is the orc warlock who leads the Burning Blade at Skull Rock, a small rebellion festering on the doorstep of Orgrimmar. He wears a pendant called the Eye of Burning Shadow, and through it an unseen voice speaks to him, demanding reports and warning him to prepare for an attack. Strangest of all, the voice threatens to set Neeru Fireblade on him if he will not answer. When the pendant was carried to Neeru, the warlock found it curious that the cult singled him out, and stranger still that the Burning Blade bears a name so close to his own.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Gazz'uz (orc warlock of the Burning Blade at Skull Rock; small rebellion on Orgrimmar's outskirts)

title: Of Age in the Valley
body: Every young orc and troll of Durotar begins in the Valley of Trials. Kaltunk looks each recruit over, laughs at their dreams of strangling dragons, and sends them to Gornek in the Den, who sighs at what the Horde has come to and sets them on boars and then on scorpids, whose antidote is made from their own venom. Smaller trials teach other lessons. Foreman Thazz'ril hands out a blackjack to wake the peons who nap among the trees, Galgar trades his famous cactus apple treat for the fruit, and a frightened peon begs someone braver to carry his food back to Razor Hill. Beneath a tree lies the wounded Hana'zua, struck down by the scorpid Sarkoth on a plateau to the south, asking only that his honor be upheld. Gornek is impressed by any recruit who will fight for a stranger's honor, and he sends aid to the wounded orc.

title: Taint in the Valley
body: Zureetha Fargaze came to the Valley of Trials to guide young recruits and found something rotten there. A group calling itself the Burning Blade had made a coven in the caves of the valley's northern cliffs, and its vile familiars were spilling out to cause havoc. She sent recruits to thin the imps first, then, guided by her divinations, sent them deep into the coven after a medallion of power held by the warlock Yarrog Baneshadow. The medallion was recovered, but Zureetha feared the cult had further aims in Durotar and that the coven was only the herald of a larger threat. She sent word to Master Gadrin at Sen'jin Village, who reported that the Burning Blade had not reached his village, though Zalazane's evil had taken root on the Echo Isles.

title: Hunting the Burning Blade
body: From Sen'jin, word of the cult went to Orgnil Soulscar in Razor Hill, who cried out that the Burning Blade was spreading and resolved to root it out. His own investigations had found the goblin warlock Fizzle Darkstorm camped in Thunder Ridge with his cultists, and his dead claw was soon brought back as proof. Next Orgnil sent his agents to the shaman Margoz, who told of a large band at Skull Rock, in the mountains just outside Orgrimmar, where cultists burned their flesh with searing collars. Margoz could not unlock the collars' secrets, so one was carried to the warlock Neeru Fireblade in the Cleft of Shadow. Neeru declared that the cult rallied around an object of demonic power called the Demon Seed, hidden in the Barrens, and that it must be destroyed.

title: The Exile of the Darkspear
body: The Echo Isles were home to the Darkspear until their own witch doctor, Zalazane, turned his voodoo on them. Driven to the mainland, the tribe still suffers him. Master Gadrin hears his dead brother Minshina calling in his dreams, his spirit chained in his own skull among others in a circle of power on the largest isle, and he begs for the skull to be brought back so the spirit can go free. Gadrin wants Zalazane himself destroyed too, along with the hexed and voodoo trolls who were once Darkspear, so that the tribe may sleep in peace. The tribe's mage Un'Thuwa senses a further wound: Zalazane's ju-ju heaps, hidden among his huts, twist the flow of magic across Durotar, corrupting beasts and feeding demons, and must be smashed before the harm becomes lasting.

title: Proudmoore's Remnant
body: Admiral Proudmoore broke the peace that Thrall had made with his daughter Jaina against Archimonde, and though the admiral is dead, his soldiers are not gone. His reserves under Lieutenant Benedict retook Tiragarde Keep, and Gar'Thok sends warriors to drive them out and prove their honor. Gar'Thok also wants the wreckage of Proudmoore's fleet searched for gnomish tools, so the Horde may learn how its enemies build their machines. From Benedict's chest comes a weathered envelope bearing the admiral's seal: orders that show his plans were laid before he died, and that more of his men may yet land. Gar'Thok, who never trusted the humans, has it carried at once to Vol'jin in Orgrimmar, who goes to counsel Thrall.

title: The Call of Earth
body: When a young orc or troll shaman in the Valley of Trials is ready, Canaga Earthcaller sends them to hunt the felstalkers for their hooves, and when they return he prepares a sapta, a draught that binds the drinker's spirit to an element. It may only be drunk in a holy place, so the novice carries it down the Hidden Path to Spirit Rock. There the earth reveals itself, and asks only humility. From it the novice receives a piece of rough quartz, small but enduring, with counsel to be patient, stay strong and seek wisdom. Canaga sets the stone at the heart of the novice's first earth totem, a focus for the powers the earth will grant as wisdom grows.
